Impute exposure values below the limit of detection

Source: R/below-lod.R
exposure_impute_lod.Rd

Environmental exposure measurements often contain values reported only as below the limit of detection (LOD), that is, left-censored values. This function replaces them by substitution, by regression on order statistics or by multiple imputation from a censored log-normal model. Missing values are kept apart from censored ones and are never imputed.

Usage

exposure_impute_lod(
  exposure_matrix,
  lod,
  method = c("lod_sqrt2", "lod_2", "ros", "multiple"),
  censored = NULL,
  M = 5L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

exposure_matrix

Numeric matrix. Rows = samples, columns = exposure variables. In the exposures named in lod, an infinite value that is not censored is an error.

lod

Named numeric vector of positive, finite detection limits, one per exposure. Names must match column names of exposure_matrix: a name that is not a column is ignored with a warning, and the function stops when no name is. Exposures not in lod are left unchanged.

method

Character. Imputation method:

"lod_sqrt2"

Substitution with LOD / sqrt(2).

"lod_2"

Substitution with LOD / 2.

"ros"

Regression on order statistics (ROS) for one detection limit per exposure; see Details.

"multiple"

Multiple imputation from a log-normal model fitted by censored maximum likelihood to a bootstrap sample of the data, as proposed by Lubin et al. (2004); returns M completed matrices.

censored

NULL (default) or a logical matrix with the same dimensions as exposure_matrix, TRUE where a value was reported as below the LOD. The numeric value at a censored position is ignored and may be NA. With NULL, a value is censored when it is not NA and is at or below the LOD. Either way, NA values that are not marked as censored are missing and stay NA.

M

Integer. Number of imputations (only for method = "multiple"). Default 5.

verbose

Logical. Report the numbers of censored and missing values per exposure. Default TRUE.

Value

For method != "multiple": the numeric matrix with censored values replaced, of the same dimensions as the input. For method = "multiple": an S4Vectors::SimpleList of M such matrices. In both cases a data.frame with one row per exposure of lod that is a column of exposure_matrix (exposure, n_detected, n_censored, n_missing, method) records what was done; it is the "lod_summary" attribute of the matrix, or metadata(result)$lod_summary for the list.

Details

Substitution is simple, but it distorts variances and associations, increasingly so as the censored fraction grows (Lubin et al. 2004).

ROS. With a single detection limit every censored value lies below every detected value, so the censored values take the lowest ranks among the non-missing values of the exposure. Blom plotting positions \((i - 3/8) / (n + 1/4)\) are computed for all \(n\) non-missing values, the logarithms of the detected values are regressed on the normal quantiles of their plotting positions, and each censored value is replaced by the value of the fitted line at one of the lowest plotting positions, capped just below the LOD (Helsel 2012). ROS reproduces the distribution of the censored values, not their individual values: the imputed values are assigned to the censored samples in row order, so they carry no information on which censored sample had the larger true value. Use the ROS values for summaries of the distribution; for association analyses prefer method = "multiple". ROS is not the reverse Kaplan-Meier estimator, which is not implemented here.

Multiple imputation. For each of the M imputations the non-missing values of an exposure are resampled with replacement, the mean and standard deviation of the log values are estimated by maximum likelihood with the censored values contributing \(P(X \le \mathrm{LOD})\), and every censored value is drawn from the fitted log-normal distribution truncated to \((0, \mathrm{LOD}]\). The bootstrap step carries the uncertainty of the fitted distribution into the imputations (Lubin et al. 2004). Analyse each completed matrix and combine the estimates with Rubin's rules (Rubin 1987). The draws use the random-number stream of the session, so call set.seed() first for reproducible imputations. If the fit fails for an exposure even on its observed values, an error names it; impute that exposure with another method.

ROS and multiple imputation assume a log-normal distribution and need at least three detected values; an exposure with fewer is imputed with LOD / sqrt(2), with a warning, and this is recorded in lod_summary. An exposure with more than 80% of its non-missing values censored gives a warning.

Other implementations: rexposome::ilod() and rexposome::imputeLOD() impute values below the LOD with the QRILC or MinProb methods of the imputeLCMD package, which are not the methods offered here.

References

Lubin JH, Colt JS, Camann D, et al. (2004). Epidemiologic evaluation of measurement data in the presence of detection limits. Environ Health Perspect 112(17):1691–1696. doi:10.1289/ehp.7199

Helsel DR (2012). Statistics for Censored Environmental Data Using Minitab and R. 2nd ed. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9781118162729

Rubin DB (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

Examples

set.seed(1)
mat <- matrix(rlnorm(200, 0, 1), nrow = 40, ncol = 5,
    dimnames = list(paste0("S", 1:40),
        c("Pb", "Cd", "Hg", "As", "BPA")))
lod <- c(Pb = 0.5, Cd = 0.3, Hg = 0.2, As = 0.1, BPA = 0.4)
## Values reported as below the LOD, and one genuinely missing value
censored <- sweep(mat, 2, lod[colnames(mat)], "<")
mat[censored] <- NA
mat["S1", "Pb"] <- NA
censored["S1", "Pb"] <- FALSE
imputed <- exposure_impute_lod(mat, lod, method = "ros",
    censored = censored)
#> Pb: 6 below LOD, 1 missing, 33 detected
#> Cd: 2 below LOD, 0 missing, 38 detected
#> Hg: 0 below LOD, 0 missing, 40 detected
#> As: 0 below LOD, 0 missing, 40 detected
#> BPA: 7 below LOD, 0 missing, 33 detected
attr(imputed, "lod_summary")
#>   exposure n_detected n_censored n_missing method
#> 1       Pb         33          6         1    ros
#> 2       Cd         38          2         0    ros
#> 3       Hg         40          0         0   none
#> 4       As         40          0         0   none
#> 5      BPA         33          7         0    ros
imputations <- exposure_impute_lod(mat, lod, method = "multiple",
    censored = censored, M = 3L, verbose = FALSE)
length(imputations)
#> [1] 3
